claims.text: Controlled oxidative annealing at 773–1173 K will selectively segregate Pt to the surface of low-Pt Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Pt nanoparticles.
The segregated Pt will form a continuous Pt-rich nanoscale surface skin.
A Pt-rich surface skin will protect the internal multi-element matrix from further oxidation.
A Pt-rich surface skin will inhibit nanoparticle sintering during catalytic operation.
The starting material consists of near-equiatomic Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Pt nanoparticles with low Pt content.
The proposed intervention is a short oxidative anneal at 773–1173 K followed by reduction.
Time-resolved in situ XPS and TEM will be used to monitor Pt segregation dynamics.
Lower Pt surface energy drives Pt segregation under oxidative conditions.
The Pt-rich layer acts as a kinetic or physical barrier to oxidation and sintering.
The Pt-rich layer preserves the structural integrity and chemical uniformity of the underlying Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Pt matrix at high temperature.
Oxidatively treated particles will have greater Pt surface enrichment than untreated particles.
Oxidatively treated particles will undergo less sintering than untreated particles during cyclic catalytic testing at 773–1173 K.
Oxidatively treated particles will undergo less phase separation than untreated particles during cyclic catalytic testing.
The untreated control will be subjected to the same thermal and catalytic conditions without the oxidative-annealing pretreatment.
The proposed stabilization mechanism applies within 773–1173 K under controlled oxidation–reduction cycling.
Temperatures substantially outside 773–1173 K or excessively long oxidation can cause unwanted sintering or failure to form the Pt-rich skin.
Multi-element mixing can promote structural stability through increased mixing entropy, lattice distortion, and sluggish diffusion that suppress phase separation and elemental segregation.
Failure to produce Pt enrichment or failure to improve structural integrity or catalytic performance relative to the untreated control would falsify the proposed Pt-skin mechanism.

contradictions.description: Describing the five-component composition as near-equiatomic while also specifying low Pt content is ambiguous and potentially inconsistent unless 'near-equiatomic' is intended to apply only to Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni.
